_comment: Copy into a workspace directory as config.json (outside any git checkout) and fill in real values. Secrets never live here: credentials are named by env var, not stored. One agent per community workspace: give each its own workspace directory and 'agent' name so their dedupe state does not collide.

source._comment: Two transports (issues #19, #45). 'agentmail' reads the workspace's own notification emails forwarded to AgentMail; 'session' reads channels as the logged-in browser user, see '_session_source_example' below. 'workspace' is a label for the Signal's source/meta fields, not a credential. Setup: turn on the workspace's own notification/digest emails and forward them to the AgentMail inbox; 'inbox' falls back to AGENTMAIL_EMAIL when omitted. 'from_contains' scopes a shared inbox to this workspace's notification sender so unrelated mail is never scored. 'channels' is a coarse substring match against subject+body (AgentMail has no structured channel field); omit for everything the digests cover. 'limit' bounds recent inbox messages per run (paged through 'next_page_token'); it is not a time window. 'include_trash' (default false) also lists messages labelled 'trash': that label can be applied outside this repo, and an inbox can look empty while holding everything the agent wants.

_session_source_example._comment: Alternative 'source' block for transport 'session' (issue #45). The framework ignores this top-level key; to use the session transport, make this object the value of 'source' in place of the agentmail block above. Reads named channels as the user logged in to the workspace in a local browser. Credentials are extracted per run from the browser cookie store (pycookiecheat, pip install '.[slack-session]') and the workspace page, held in memory and dropped at exit; nothing is stored and nothing is configured here. On macOS the cookie decryption reads the login keychain and may prompt the first time. Read-only: the client refuses any Slack method outside a fixed allowlist (auth.test, conversations.list/info/history/replies, chat.getPermalink, users.info, users.list) before any HTTP; no config key widens it. 'subdomain' is the <subdomain> in <subdomain>.slack.com and must be a workspace you are logged in to in 'browser' (pycookiecheat name: chrome (default), chromium, brave, firefox, slack). 'channels' entries are names without '#', resolved to ids per run (an unknown name raises and lists what the workspace has), or conversation ids used directly: C/G for a channel and D for a direct message, which has no name to resolve. An id costs one conversations.info call for the meta.channel label, which for a DM is the other member's display name. 'from_users' (optional) keeps only messages from those user ids, which is what makes a bot's DM usable: the conversation also holds your own replies. It applies to thread replies too, so a kept message folds in only the replies from a wanted author, and a parent whose replies are all filtered out folds nothing. 'since_hours' is the conversations.history lookback; Signal ids are <channel_id>:<ts>, so overlapping windows dedupe through the SeenStore. 'include_threads' folds thread replies into the parent message's text. A channel whose history is capped by the workspace's plan (Slack's free-tier visibility limit) raises rather than returning a partial window.
